findings.location: Qualification command contract and Security contract
findings.affected_requirement: The analyze gate must confirm consistency across spec.md, the complete plan set, and tasks.md; a plan-accepted checkpoint requires the complete planning artifact set to align with the accepted plan before tasks advance.
findings.evidence: The current supporting contract still defines qualification through `cgc --context <run-context> query` at specs/001-codegraph-extraction/contracts/repository-profiling-api.md:58 and explicitly says no `cgc api` command is allowed at specs/001-codegraph-extraction/contracts/repository-profiling-api.md:122. The accepted revised plan and regenerated tasks instead require `cgc api start`, `GET /health`, and `POST /api/v1/query` in specs/001-codegraph-extraction/plan.md:124, specs/001-codegraph-extraction/plan.md:126, and specs/001-codegraph-extraction/tasks.md:48. specs/001-codegraph-extraction/reviews/plan-review-4.json accepted only plan.md plus the change proposal in its owned boundary, so this contradictory supporting artifact was not independently re-accepted with the HTTP JSON revision.
findings.correction_outcome: Regenerate and independently review the full revised plan set so every planning artifact that defines the qualification contract reflects the approved HTTP JSON lifecycle before implementation resumes.

findings.affected_requirement: workflow-state.json is the canonical resumable workflow state; after task generation the current stage and next required steps must accurately represent the artifact boundary being analyzed.
findings.evidence: The state still declares top-level stage `plan` and lists `fresh-task-generation` plus `speckit-analyze` as next steps, while the current workspace already contains a regenerated qualification-only tasks.md and this fresh analyze boundary. The same file's persisted checkpoint and timestamp remain tied to the prior analyze cycle.
findings.correction_outcome: When this analyze result is persisted, synchronize workflow-state.json to the regenerated tasks/analyze boundary so resume and later gating use the current artifact set.

summary: The regenerated task graph is still correctly bounded to qualification-only work: it preserves the single replacement provider gate, forbids retry, and routes pass/fail back to later planning or corrective planning rather than production implementation. The gate cannot return ACCEPT because the current plan set is not internally consistent: repository-profiling-api.md still encodes the superseded CLI-query qualification contract and forbids `cgc api`, while plan.md and tasks.md now depend on the approved local HTTP JSON lifecycle. workflow-state.json also required synchronization to the regenerated tasks/analyze boundary.

coverage_observations.spec_phase_boundary: The broader Story 4.1 specification remains intentionally larger than the current execution slice, and the plan explicitly phases execution behind provider qualification first.
coverage_observations.qualification_stop_condition: Tasks T009-T010 correctly stop after one replacement provider execution and do not authorize production adapter, persistence, migration, Git/API/UI/E2E, Worker Agent, Scan Coordinator, Uncertainty, or Cross-Repository Resolution work.
coverage_observations.review_coverage_gap: The accepted revision review did not independently cover the full revised plan set, which allowed a stale supporting contract artifact to remain in contradiction with the approved HTTP JSON transport.

artifact_hash_coverage.note: No live hash-computation tool was available in this read-only session. Historical hashes exist inside workflow-state.json, but they were not treated as current-boundary artifact hashes for this verdict.
